# Review of the plausibility (a reader of the texts)

## Summary

Read as a scholar of the works would read it, the draft is careful: it attributes the later period's fear vocabulary to Jekyll and Hyde and says the topics are the works.

## Points to address

1. The dialogue words as key terms fit the later works' narration (Poole and Utterson's exchanges, the Yellow Wallpaper's diary); say so as an interpretation.
2. Usher's high rate is no surprise for a Gothic tale; the draft could name it as the earlier period's counterpart of Jekyll and Hyde.
